name: vn-en-eval-set-v2
description: VN→EN correction eval set v2 — 60 pairs filling coverage gaps from v1: literal_translation, omission, register, redundancy, B2/C1 CEFR, multi-tag, formal/professional contexts

entries.input: Can you explain for me this word?
entries.expected: Can you explain this word to me?
entries.vietlishPattern: giải thích cho tôi → 'explain for me' — Vietnamese bổ ngữ gián tiếp giữ 'cho' → inserted 'for' before indirect object instead of 'to' after direct object

entries.input: I want to inform to you that the meeting is canceled.
entries.expected: I want to inform you that the meeting has been canceled.
entries.vietlishPattern: thông báo cho bạn → 'inform to you' — Vietnamese thông báo + cho mirrors French/VN indirect object marker; English 'inform' takes bare indirect object

entries.input: Please let me know your think about this proposal.
entries.expected: Please let me know your thoughts on this proposal.
entries.vietlishPattern: suy nghĩ của bạn → 'your think' — suy nghĩ is both verb and noun in Vietnamese; learner carries verb form into noun slot; 'thoughts' plural expected in English

entries.input: I have a meeting with my boss in next Monday.
entries.expected: I have a meeting with my boss next Monday.
entries.vietlishPattern: vào thứ Hai tới → 'in next Monday' — vào signals time in Vietnamese but 'next Monday' needs no preposition in English

entries.input: She is very boring because she has nothing to do.
entries.expected: She is very bored because she has nothing to do.
entries.vietlishPattern: rất chán → 'very boring' — Vietnamese chán is state (bored), not property (boring); -ed/-ing participial adjective distinction absent in Vietnamese

entries.input: I am interesting in learning English.
entries.expected: I am interested in learning English.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi thích / tôi quan tâm → 'I am interesting' — -ed state vs -ing property confusion; Vietnamese không phân biệt hai dạng này

entries.input: He suggested me to apply for that job.
entries.expected: He suggested that I apply for that job.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy gợi ý tôi → 'suggested me to' — Vietnamese gợi ý + object mirrors 'advise/tell + object + to-inf' pattern; 'suggest' in English requires that-clause or gerund

entries.input: My company has three branch in Ho Chi Minh City.
entries.expected: My company has three branches in Ho Chi Minh City.
entries.vietlishPattern: ba chi nhánh → no plural suffix in Vietnamese; numeral already marks plurality; learner omits English -s

entries.input: I was born in Hanoi. My family is living there for 20 years.
entries.expected: I was born in Hanoi. My family has been living there for 20 years.
entries.vietlishPattern: đã sống ở đó 20 năm → present progressive instead of present perfect continuous; Vietnamese tense conveyed by time adverb 'đã' without aspect change in verb

entries.input: Please reply this email when you receive it.
entries.expected: Please reply to this email when you receive it.
entries.vietlishPattern: trả lời email này → 'reply this email' — Vietnamese phúc đáp + direct object; English 'reply' is intransitive, requires 'reply to + object'

entries.input: He is absent today because he is sick.
entries.expected: He is absent today because he is sick.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: common causal structure; 'because' clause grammatically complete; no correction needed

entries.input: I need you to explain more clearly.
entries.expected: I need you to explain more clearly.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: 'need + object + to-inf + adverb' is grammatical; no correction needed

entries.input: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?
entries.expected: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: common polite request; correct use of 'borrow'; no correction needed

entries.input: The weather is very hot today, isn't it?
entries.expected: The weather is very hot today, isn't it?
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: correct tag question form; no correction needed

entries.input: She told me that she would come back soon.
entries.expected: She told me that she would come back soon.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: correct backshift in reported speech; no correction needed

entries.input: I wish I can speak English fluently.
entries.expected: I wish I could speak English fluently.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi ước tôi có thể → 'I wish I can' — Vietnamese ước + có thể doesn't shift modality; English subjunctive/unreal conditional requires 'could' in wish-clause

entries.input: If I will have more time, I will study abroad.
entries.expected: If I had more time, I would study abroad.
entries.vietlishPattern: nếu tôi có nhiều thời gian hơn → 'if I will have' — Vietnamese nếu clause uses present/future form; English counterfactual if-clause requires past tense

entries.input: The problem was discuss in the meeting.
entries.expected: The problem was discussed in the meeting.
entries.vietlishPattern: vấn đề được thảo luận → 'was discuss' — Vietnamese passive với 'được' + bare verb root; English passive requires past participle

entries.input: This is the book which I told you about it.
entries.expected: This is the book that I told you about.
entries.vietlishPattern: quyển sách mà tôi đã nói với bạn về nó → 'about it' — Vietnamese relativization retains pronoun copy ('về nó'); English stranded preposition drops the resumptive pronoun

entries.input: He is the person that I met him at the conference.
entries.expected: He is the person that I met at the conference.
entries.vietlishPattern: người mà tôi gặp anh ấy → resumptive pronoun 'him' kept inside relative clause; Vietnamese cho phép đại từ tóm lại; English prohibits resumptive pronouns in relative clauses

entries.input: I have already finished the report already.
entries.expected: I have already finished the report.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi đã hoàn thành báo cáo rồi → double already ('already...already' or 'đã...rồi') — Vietnamese uses 'đã' (beginning) + 'rồi' (end) to mark perfective; learner mirrors both markers

entries.input: She return home late last night.
entries.expected: She returned home late last night.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy về nhà muộn → bare verb in past context; 'last night' marks past but Vietnamese không biến đổi động từ

entries.input: My mother, she works as a nurse in the hospital.
entries.expected: My mother works as a nurse in the hospital.
entries.vietlishPattern: mẹ tôi, bà ấy làm y tá → left-dislocation with topic pronoun — Vietnamese topic-comment structure keeps subject pronoun after topic; English drops the pronoun copy

entries.input: The food in this restaurant, it is very delicious.
entries.expected: The food in this restaurant is very delicious.
entries.vietlishPattern: đồ ăn ở đây, nó ngon lắm → topic pronoun 'it' duplicates subject; Vietnamese topic-comment keeps pronoun; English drops resumptive 'it'

entries.input: I don't know about it.
entries.expected: I don't know about it.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable variant: 'don't know about it' is standard informal English; no correction needed

entries.input: Please write your name in this form.
entries.expected: Please write your name on this form.
entries.vietlishPattern: điền tên trong mẫu → 'in this form' — Vietnamese 'trong' (inside) used for forms/documents; English 'on' collocates with form/paper surface

entries.input: She is depend on her parents for money.
entries.expected: She depends on her parents for money.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy phụ thuộc → 'is depend' — copula 'is' inserted before bare verb instead of conjugated form; Vietnamese linking verb không có dạng biến đổi

entries.input: We must to submit the report by Friday.
entries.expected: We must submit the report by Friday.
entries.vietlishPattern: chúng ta phải nộp → 'must to submit' — Vietnamese phải + bare verb form; learner inserts 'to' treating 'must' like other modals (have to, need to, want to)

entries.input: I suggest to take the train instead of the bus.
entries.expected: I suggest taking the train instead of the bus.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi đề nghị đi tàu → 'suggest to take' — Vietnamese gợi ý/đề nghị + bare verb; English 'suggest' requires gerund or that-clause, never to-infinitive

entries.input: He made me to feel better.
entries.expected: He made me feel better.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy làm tôi cảm thấy → 'made me to feel' — causative 'make' takes bare infinitive, not to-infinitive; learner over-applies 'to' pattern from want/expect/encourage

entries.input: I am looking forward to meet you next week.
entries.expected: I am looking forward to meeting you next week.
entries.vietlishPattern: mong được gặp bạn → 'look forward to meet' — Vietnamese mong + bare verb; 'to' in 'look forward to' is a preposition not an infinitive marker, requires gerund

entries.input: She entered to the room quietly.
entries.expected: She entered the room quietly.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy bước vào phòng → 'entered to the room' — Vietnamese vào requires directional complement; 'enter' is transitive in English, no preposition needed

entries.input: I need more information about the product before I make my decision.
entries.expected: I need more information about the product before I make my decision.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: complete, grammatical, appropriately formal sentence; no correction needed

entries.input: He didn't mention about the issue in the report.
entries.expected: He didn't mention the issue in the report.
entries.vietlishPattern: không đề cập đến vấn đề → 'mention about' — Vietnamese đề cập + đến (directional); English 'mention' is transitive, no preposition; 'mention about' is a common non-native pattern

entries.input: The applicant lacks of relevant experience for this role.
entries.expected: The applicant lacks relevant experience for this role.
entries.vietlishPattern: thiếu kinh nghiệm → 'lacks of' — Vietnamese thiếu + noun is fine; English 'lack' is transitive, no 'of'; contrasted with 'lack of' as a noun phrase

entries.input: We need to discuss about the project timeline urgently.
entries.expected: We need to discuss the project timeline urgently.
entries.vietlishPattern: cần thảo luận về → 'discuss about' — Vietnamese thảo luận + về; English 'discuss' is transitive; 'about' is redundant (unlike 'talk about' which needs the preposition)

entries.input: I hope that you will consider my application favorably.
entries.expected: I hope that you will consider my application favorably.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: formal closing line; correct conditional structure; no correction needed

entries.input: Please be advised that failure to comply may result consequences.
entries.expected: Please be advised that failure to comply may result in consequences.
entries.vietlishPattern: dẫn đến hậu quả → 'result consequences' — 'result' is intransitive; requires 'result in'; Vietnamese dẫn đến is a transitive verb phrase, learner omits English preposition

entries.input: I agree your point about the budget.
entries.expected: I agree with your point about the budget.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi đồng ý ý kiến của bạn → 'agree your point' — Vietnamese đồng ý + noun (no preposition needed); English 'agree' is intransitive, requires 'agree with + noun'

entries.input: She is good cooking Vietnamese food.
entries.expected: She is good at cooking Vietnamese food.
entries.vietlishPattern: cô ấy giỏi nấu ăn → 'good cooking' — Vietnamese giỏi + bare verb/noun; English 'good at' requires preposition 'at' before gerund

entries.input: He is responsible the project management.
entries.expected: He is responsible for the project management.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy chịu trách nhiệm quản lý dự án → 'responsible + noun' — Vietnamese chịu trách nhiệm + bare noun; English 'responsible for' requires preposition

entries.input: I would like to apologize the inconvenience caused.
entries.expected: I would like to apologize for the inconvenience caused.
entries.vietlishPattern: xin lỗi sự bất tiện → 'apologize the inconvenience' — Vietnamese xin lỗi + direct object; English 'apologize for' is intransitive + 'for' preposition

entries.input: We are looking a solution to this technical issue.
entries.expected: We are looking for a solution to this technical issue.
entries.vietlishPattern: đang tìm giải pháp → 'looking a solution' — Vietnamese tìm kiếm + direct object; English 'look for' is a phrasal verb requiring 'for'

entries.input: She never complains her situation and always stays positive.
entries.expected: She never complains about her situation and always stays positive.
entries.vietlishPattern: không bao giờ phàn nàn về → 'complains her situation' — Vietnamese phàn nàn can take direct object colloquially; English 'complain about' requires preposition

entries.input: He arrived at the office on time, despite the heavy traffic.
entries.expected: He arrived at the office on time, despite the heavy traffic.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: correct 'despite + noun phrase'; correct 'arrived at' collocation; no correction needed

entries.input: The manager wants everyone to attend the meeting and to be prepared.
entries.expected: The manager wants everyone to attend the meeting and to be prepared.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: parallel infinitive construction is natural; 'to attend...and to be' both acceptable; no correction needed

entries.input: The policy is apply to all employees without exception.
entries.expected: The policy applies to all employees without exception.
entries.vietlishPattern: chính sách được áp dụng → 'is apply' — Vietnamese passive 'được áp dụng'; learner produces passive copula + bare verb instead of active third-person singular form

entries.input: Under no circumstances we should accept this offer.
entries.expected: Under no circumstances should we accept this offer.
entries.vietlishPattern: trong mọi trường hợp chúng ta không nên → subject-first word order after fronted negative; English requires subject-auxiliary inversion after negative fronting ('Under no circumstances should we...')

entries.input: Had I known the truth earlier, I would have acted differently.
entries.expected: Had I known the truth earlier, I would have acted differently.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: inverted conditional perfect (Had I known...) — advanced but grammatical; no correction needed

entries.input: Not only he came late, but also he forgot the documents.
entries.expected: Not only did he come late, but he also forgot the documents.
entries.vietlishPattern: không những anh ấy đến trễ, mà còn... → no inversion after 'not only'; English requires do-support inversion in the first clause after fronted 'not only'

entries.input: Seldom we have seen such dedication in a new employee.
entries.expected: Seldom have we seen such dedication in a new employee.
entries.vietlishPattern: hiếm khi chúng tôi thấy → no inversion after fronted negative adverb 'seldom'; English requires auxiliary inversion: 'Seldom have we seen'

entries.input: It was until I read the report that I understood the full picture.
entries.expected: It was not until I read the report that I understood the full picture.
entries.vietlishPattern: mãi đến khi tôi đọc báo cáo → 'it was until' — the cleft structure requires 'It was not until...that'; Vietnamese 'mãi đến khi' carries the negative implicitly; learner omits 'not'

entries.input: The report, which submitted last week, has been reviewed by the committee.
entries.expected: The report, which was submitted last week, has been reviewed by the committee.
entries.vietlishPattern: báo cáo được nộp tuần trước → omitted auxiliary 'was' in relative clause passive; Vietnamese passive 'được nộp' uses single auxiliary; English passive requires 'was/were + past participle'

entries.input: He spoke very professionally during the interview, which impressed the panel.
entries.expected: He spoke very professionally during the interview, which impressed the panel.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: non-restrictive relative clause 'which' correctly refers to entire clause; no correction needed

entries.input: The feedback from customer is very important for us improve our service.
entries.expected: Feedback from customers is very important for us to improve our service.
entries.vietlishPattern: phản hồi từ khách hàng quan trọng để chúng tôi cải thiện → multiple omissions: 'for us' requires 'for us to' (to-infinitive); 'feedback' usually uncountable no article; 'customer' → 'customers' (generic plural)

entries.input: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction regarding the service I received on June 5.
entries.expected: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction regarding the service I received on June 5.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: formal complaint register; correct preposition 'regarding'; no correction needed

entries.input: You should have told me earlier. Now it is too late to make a change.
entries.expected: You should have told me earlier. Now it is too late to make a change.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: correct past modal perfect 'should have told'; natural cause-effect structure; no correction needed

entries.input: Despite of the difficulties, she managed to complete the project on time.
entries.expected: Despite the difficulties, she managed to complete the project on time.
entries.vietlishPattern: mặc dù những khó khăn → 'Despite of' — confusion with 'in spite of'; 'despite' does not take 'of'; Vietnamese 'mặc dù' + noun doesn't signal this distinction

entries.input: The staff were informed in advance, so no one was surprise.
entries.expected: The staff were informed in advance, so no one was surprised.
entries.vietlishPattern: không ai ngạc nhiên → 'was surprise' — bare adjective/verb form; Vietnamese trạng thái không biến đổi; English passive adjective requires -ed form 'surprised'

entries.input: Her presentation was so clear that even the non-technical staff could understand it.
entries.expected: Her presentation was so clear that even the non-technical staff could understand it.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: correct 'so...that' result clause; 'even' correctly placed before noun; no correction needed
